title: SLO Experimentation, Controlled Degradation & Logbook
author: Janelle Park
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood's structured approach for running SLO-driven experiments that intentionally degrade user-facing capacity/quality in a safe, observable, and auditable way. It includes a prescriptive checklist, an experiment logbook format, error-budget decision rules, telemetry expectations, and step-by-step procedures for controlled degradations and rollbacks.

Intent and scope:
- Intent: enable Product, SRE, and Platform teams to conduct capacity and degradation experiments (canaries, load-shedding, quantization trials, cache eviction tests) while protecting customers and preserving incident evidence.
- Scope: applies to all production and staging clusters serving live inference traffic (hosted API + Dedicated pools). Not for internal dev sandboxes unless explicitly approved.

Key definitions:
- Experiment: any planned action that alters serving behavior to test SLO and capacity hypotheses (e.g., increasing batching, toggling quantization, enabling fallback model).
- Controlled degradation: deterministic reduction of service quality or capacity (graceful fallback, limited token cap, synthetic latency injection) used in experiments or emergency throttles.
- Logbook entry: canonical record for each experiment (metadata, expected impact, rollback plan, telemetry links).

Ownership and approvals:
- Experiment owner: engineering or product engineer sponsoring the experiment. Responsible for runbook authoring and post-run analysis.
- SRE reviewer: must be an on-call SRE or capacity steward; approves runway and rollback before execution.
- Platform owner: signs off on infra-level changes (autoscaler rules, kernel flags).

Pre-experiment checklist (all items must be green):
1) Hypothesis documented and linked to an SLO metric (e.g., 99th p99 latency, error-rate).
2) Expected delta: quantitative estimate of SLO and cost impact (tokens/sec, latency ms, cost $/100k tokens).
3) Error budget status: ensure cumulative burn + planned impact keeps service above soft-safety threshold (<= 40% of budget burn for high-impact experiments).
4) Stakeholder notice: pager, product, account managers notified via email and #sre-experiments channel at least 48 hours prior (or 4 hours for low-risk).
5) Observability hooks in place: dashboards, dashboards watchlist, synthetic canaries, request/response sampling enabled.
6) Rollback & mitigation steps validated in staging and dry-run approved.
7) Throttle and priority lanes configured; emergency manual throttle documented and tested.
8) Compliance and data residency implications reviewed (security approval if required).

Experiment logbook template (single-line delimited fields for easy ingestion):
- experiment_id: SLE-YYYYMMDD-<short>
- owner: <name>
- runbook_link: <confluence url>
- hypothesis: <one sentence>
- target_slo: <metric, target>
- expected_impact: <percent or absolute>
- start_window: <UTC window>
- rollback_thresholds: <metric:threshold>
- telemetry_links: <comma-separated grafana/prometheus/synthetic>
- pre_checks_passed: yes/no
- result_summary: <pass/fail/partial>
- postmortem_link: <confluence url>

Error budget governance rules (quick reference):
- Green: budget burn <= 10% in last 7d — experiment may proceed with standard approvals.
- Caution: 10% < burn <= 40% — require SRE reviewer + limited blast radius (canary lane only).
- Halt: burn > 40% — disallow non-emergency degradations; any experiment must be coordinated with product and paused.

Capacity & telemetry signal table (expected channels and thresholds):
| Signal | PromQL example | Alert threshold | Use in experiment |
|--------|----------------|----------------|-------------------|
| p99_latency | histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) | > 1200ms | rollback if crossed |
| request_error_rate | sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) | > 0.02 | escalate, abort experiment |
| gpu_mem_pressure | avg(gpu_memory_used_bytes/gpu_memory_total_bytes) | > 0.85 | reduce batch size |
| token_queue_depth | avg(inference_queue_length[1m]) | > 200 | enable extra queue draining |

Controlled degradation runbook (ordered steps):
1) Pre-window: create logbook entry and link to SLO dashboards.
2) Notify stakeholders: post start ETA in #sre-experiments and update incident cadence board.
3) Baseline capture (5–15 min): run synthetic canary and export baseline metrics.
4) Execute ramp plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% of target change each 10 minutes, with SRE sign-off between phases.
5) Observe for threshold violations during each ramp. If any rollback_threshold trips, immediately roll back to previous stable percentage and hold for 10 minutes for signal stabilization.
6) If progressive ramps complete and metrics match hypothesis, run a 30–60 minute steady window for confirmation.
7) Execute final rollback to full production or implement approved configuration permanently if post-run analysis indicates safe improvement.
8) Close logbook entry and schedule postmortem analysis within 7 calendar days.

Emergency abort and manual throttle (fast path):
- Trigger: prioritized pager, or any alert crossing the Halt threshold.
- Action: run the emergency CLI to reassign priority lanes and apply immediate token cap:

CLI example:
- Reassign priority lane: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/priorities -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"service":"inference","priority_map":{"premium":0.8,"standard":0.15,"free":0.05}}'
- Apply token cap: rwdctl throttle set --service inference --cap-tokens 128 --scope region-us-east-1

Observability & evidence requirements (minimum):
- Always capture: raw request trace samples (1/1000 or higher for p99 experiments), error logs (structured JSON), and KV-cache hit/miss rates.
- Tag traces with experiment_id and owner.
- Retain synthetic canary traces and aggregated telemetry for at least 14 days for experiments.

Post-experiment analysis checklist:
1) Confirm whether the hypothesis was validated; include numeric delta vs baseline.
2) Map experiment impact to SLO burn using the SLO accounting workbook.
3) Identify any unintended side effects (increased tail latency for embeddings, cache pressure).
4) Decide: revert, patch, or promote to feature flag. If promote, create deployment PR with required sizing changes.
5) Author a short runbook entry that captures the safe operating point and rollback actions for the change.

Incident review & evidence linkage:
- All experiments that caused an SLO breach must invoke a standard incident review. The logbook entry should be linked from the incident review page and preserved as digital evidence.
- Add the tag "experiment-evidence" to incident artifacts so automated tools can surface them for postmortem analysis.

Tooling integrations (recommended):
- SLO Accounting workbook (Sheets) — template link: /sheets/slo-accounting-template
- Experiment log ingestion: a lightweight service (sre-experiments-api) that accepts the logbook template as CSV/JSON. Use SSE to stream events into the audit index.
- Dashboard templates: cloneable Grafana panel: "experiment watchlist" with p50/p95/p99, error-rate, queue depth, and cost-per-token series.

Appendix A — sample JSON logbook entry (single-line compact):
{"experiment_id":"SLE-20260301-quantize-a","owner":"janelle.park","runbook_link":"/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/slo-experimentation-degradation-logbook-2026","hypothesis":"8-bit quantization reduces token cost by 20% with <5% p99 latency regression","target_slo":"p99_latency<=1000ms","expected_impact":"-20% cost, +3% p99 latency","start_window":"2026-03-05T10:00:00Z/2026-03-05T12:00:00Z","rollback_thresholds":"p99_latency:>1200ms,request_error_rate:>0.02","telemetry_links":"grafana/d/abc, prometheus/expr/xyz","pre_checks_passed":"yes","result_summary":"pending","postmortem_link":""}

Appendix B — responsible contacts and escalation matrix:
- Primary SRE reviewer: on-call SRE (see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-roster)
- Capacity owner: Miguel Ortega (platform-capacity)
- Product sponsor: add product PM assigned to experiment
